question: On Bank of America's second-quarter 2026 earnings call (July 14, 2026), what full-year 2026 outlook did the CFO give for (a) net interest income (NII) growth and (b) operating leverage, and how did each compare with the outlook he said had been given earlier in 2026 (in January and/or April)?
grading: Key points (all required): (1) full-year 2026 NII growth expected at the UPPER END of the 6%-8% range (not a new numeric range); (2) full-year 2026 operating leverage expected in the range of 300 to 400 basis points; (3) comparison with earlier outlook: NII growth was 5%-7% in January and raised to 6%-8% in April; operating leverage was 'more than 200 basis points' as of the April (Q1) call. Accept equivalent wording ('top end of 6-8%', '3-4 percentage points'). Fail if the answer gives plain 6%-8% or 5%-7% as the current NII view without 'upper end', gives 'more than 200 bps' as the current operating-leverage view, states a dollar NII figure as guidance, or relies on remarks from the Q3 2026 call (mid-October 2026, after the as_of date) or the mid-September Barclays conference.
answer: (a) Full-year 2026 NII growth is now expected at the upper end of the 6%-8% range (the CFO recalled 5%-7% in January, raised to 6%-8% in April) [W01-E1]. (b) Full-year 2026 operating leverage is now expected to be 300 to 400 basis points, up from 'more than 200 basis points' given on the April call; first-half 2026 operating leverage had already exceeded 450 bps (Q2: 6.6%) [W01-E1]. Neither full-year outlook appears in the July 14 press release or in the slide deck filed with the 8-K [W01-E2, W01-E3].

**Interpreted as:** 'Second-quarter 2026 earnings call' read as BAC's Q2 FY2026 (quarter ended 2026-06-30) call held 2026-07-14, matching the 8-K earnings release date. Full-year 2026 = fiscal year ending 2026-12-31 (BAC's fiscal year is the calendar year). NII growth read as the CFO's stated full-year 2026 net interest income (GAAP, FTE basis as the company guides) growth versus 2025. Operating leverage read as the CFO's stated full-year 2026 operating leverage (revenue growth less expense growth) outlook. 'Earlier in 2026' read as the outlooks given on the Q4 2025 call (January 2026) and the Q1 2026 call (April 2026); both are compared where stated.

- The only full-year 2026 net interest income growth outlook in the evidence is the one reported by CNBC on April 15, 2026 (Q1 FY2026 results day), when Bank of America raised its full-year 2026 NII growth guidance to between 6% and 8%, up from a prior projection of between 5% and 7%. [1]
- The evidence does not attribute the April 2026 full-year 2026 NII growth guidance to the CFO by name; CNBC describes it as the bank's guidance, and the Q1 FY2026 8-K release (filed 2026-04-15) contains no full-year NII growth or operating leverage outlook. [1][2]

**Not available**
- CFO's full-year 2026 net interest income growth outlook given on the Q2 FY2026 earnings call (July 14, 2026): The evidence contains BAC's Q2 FY2026 8-K earnings release, presentation and supplemental information (all filed 2026-07-14) plus XBRL data, but no transcript or coverage of the July 14, 2026 earnings call, so the CFO's call commentary on full-year 2026 NII growth is not present. [3][4][5]
- CFO's full-year 2026 operating leverage outlook given on the Q2 FY2026 earnings call (July 14, 2026): No call transcript or coverage is provided; the Q2 FY2026 materials report only the quarterly operating leverage of 6.6% for 2Q26, not a full-year 2026 operating leverage outlook. [3][4]

[3][4][5]
- Full-year 2026 operating leverage outlook given earlier in 2026 (January 2026 Q4 2025 call and/or April 2026 Q1 2026 call): The evidence provides only quarterly operating leverage figures (e.g., 2.9% for 1Q26 and 6.6% for 2Q26) and no full-year 2026 operating leverage guidance from either the January or April 2026 calls. [2][6][3][4]
- CFO's full-year 2026 NII growth outlook given on the January 2026 Q4 2025 earnings call: The January 14, 2026 Q4 2025 release and the CNBC preview of that date do not state a full-year 2026 NII growth outlook; the 5%-7% prior projection is referenced only retrospectively in the April 15, 2026 CNBC article, without attribution to the January call or the CFO.
